summary: Customer disputes status page accuracy during us-east degradation (status showed Operational while streaming requests failed)
description:
Customer (Lattice Financial) reports that during the 2025-11-07 us-east degradation they experienced elevated errors and streaming disconnects, but our public status page showed "Operational" for the relevant timeframe. Customer is requesting (a) confirmation that Redwood recognizes the outage and (b) clarification on why the status page did not reflect the impact.

Issue summary:
- Customer observed: intermittent 5xx/stream resets on streaming chat completions in us-east; elevated end-user error rates.
- Redwood status page observed by customer: "All Systems Operational" (no component marked degraded/outage until after their peak impact window).
- Customer concern: status page is too coarse (global/hosted API only) and/or incorrectly classified impact (streaming vs non-streaming, per-region impact not reflected).

Impact (customer-reported):
- Duration: ~20–30 minutes (approx 16:05–16:35 UTC per customer); residual retries for another ~10 minutes.
- Symptoms: SSE stream dropped mid-response; some requests returned 502/504; retries succeeded.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (stream=true).

What we need to do:
1) Validate the timeframe and whether our internal incident timeline matches customer evidence.
2) Provide a customer-facing explanation for the status page mismatch without disclosing sensitive capacity/customer-specific details.
3) Capture action items feeding into the status page transparency upgrades project (component taxonomy + signal mapping + comms process).

Customer-provided artifacts (summarized):
- Request IDs: LF-7b2c1e, LF-7b2c33, LF-7b2c8a (sample)
- Error codes: 502/504; stream disconnect without final event.
- Region: us-east only (customer also has low-volume eu-west traffic not impacted).

Internal notes:
- Internal incident opened: INC-2025-1107-USE1-STREAMING (SRE).
- Public status page components at time were too coarse (Hosted API global), and our automated classifier did not mark the correct component/region promptly.
- Known gap tracked by SRE: inability to represent "Streaming (us-east)" separately from "Hosted API"; led to delayed and ambiguous external comms.

Requested outcome for closure:
- Provide written acknowledgement + corrected timeline to customer.
- Share our planned improvements: new component granularity (product surface + region), standard comms templates, and faster time-to-first-update goals.
- Confirm whether any post-incident summary will be published and when.

Assigning Rachel Kim (Ent CS) and looping SRE on-call for evidence + timeline. Related internal incident per #incidents: INC-2025-1107-USE1-STREAMING.

Status page update was delayed due to component ambiguity (only "Hosted API" global component) and incomplete signal mapping for streaming-specific metrics by region.

It demonstrates the need for: Hosted API vs Streaming separation; per-region visibility; and clear guidance on when to mark "Degraded Performance" vs "Partial Outage" for latency/disconnect-heavy events.

resolution: Resolved customer dispute by providing verified internal incident timeline and acknowledging a status page mismatch due to overly coarse components and incomplete streaming/region signal mapping. Customer accepted explanation. Follow-ups captured for the status page transparency upgrades initiative: implement per-capability/per-region components (including Streaming us-east), improve signal-to-component mapping to prevent misclassification, and standardize incident update templates + approval flow for faster time-to-first-update.
